subject: parameter estimates for missing cells in multipleGroup

messages.author: 46f0a61cd2366351
messages.subject: parameter estimates for missing cells in multipleGroup
parts:
I am working on a multiple group model where some items are not administered to one of the groups. When I run this model with missing data coded as "NA", I still get coefficient estimates for the item/group cell with all missing data. I am not sure where this estimate is coming from or if I can trust the parameter estimates for the other items/groups. An example of this problem is given below.



library(mirt)

dat <- expand.table(LSAT6)

model <- "F = 1-5
          CONSTRAIN = (1, d), (1,2,3,4,5, a1)
          CONSTRAINB = (1, d), (1,2,3,4,5, a1)"

## pretend that this is multiple group data
gp <- factor(c(rep(0, 500), rep(1, 500)))

## suppose group 1 is not administered item 5
dat$Item_5[gp == 1] <- NA


mod <- multipleGroup(data = dat, model = model, group = gp,
                     invariance = c('free_means','free_var','slopes'),
                     technical = list(NCYCLES = 3300))



coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'0'$items
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'1'$items
## for group "1", gives an estimate for Item_5

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: parameter estimates for missing cells in multipleGroup
parts:
Hi Leah,

This topic has come up a few times before in relation to 'vertical scaling' where groups are administered a set of different and common items in order to equate the groups based on common items (a missingness-by-design situation). I'll use this topic as a springboard into what's happening here and how these coefs should be interpreted (*spoiler*, the coefs are fine, and so are their standard errors). 

Consider the following design:

------------------------------------
Group   Set-1  Set-2  Set-3
------------------------------------
G1           NA      1         0
G1           NA      1         1
G1           NA      0         1
------------------------------------
G2             1       0        NA
G2             0       1        NA
G2             1       0        NA
------------------------------------

In this design there are three individuals in each group, and NA's indicate that they did not answer the item. Here, only Set-2 is in common because Set-1 and 3 are either answered by G2 only (Set-1) or G1 only (Set-3). Hence, if you were to try and fit single group IRT models (e.g., with mirt() after using subset() on the respective data) then the function will complain saying something like 'an item contains completely missing data and is therefore useless'. multipleGroup() takes a slightly different look though, but is equivalent when thinking in terms of the likelihood functions.

As a prelude to be explained momentarily, it is imperative that all parameters in Set-1 and Set-3 be constrained to be equal across groups. This is because without this equality constraint the optimizer will essentially think that G1 contains enough information to estimate the associated group-partitioned parameters using only the subsetted data relevant to G1 and G2 (which they does not, as they only contains NAs in certain blocks). In fact, if you did not constrain the parameters across groups then the algorithms will almost surely spin out of control because the model will be badly identified. 

So, when you constrain Set-1 and 3's parameters to be equal across groups you will get equal estimates for G1 and G2, however all the information about these parameters comes from the groups with the actual observed data. Hence, although there was no data for G1 in Set-1 all the information from the parameters came from the data in G2; so in essence the parameters completely borrowed the strength where data was available. Standard errors are only based on locations where data came from as well, and the coefs where groups contained no data are fine and essentially ghosted in from the available information due to the equality constraints. 

I hope that makes sense, but please let me know if this still requires more clarification. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: parameter estimates for missing cells in multipleGroup
parts:
Hi Leah,

It looks like for this example there are still slopes constrained to be equal across the groups, so that provides a bit of stability (however I would disagree the parameters look okay; the intercept for the missing data item is rather large). Also, the fact that the model took more that 500 cycles is also an indication that something is probably wrong. 

That being said, if you pass SE = TRUE you get a note that the model is not empirically identified. This is generally why if you aren't sure whether a model is identified it's good practice to estimate the ACOV matrix as a second-order identification test (it should be positive definite in order to obtain standard errors). Cheers.

Phil

parts:
Phil,

Ah, I see now that I may have omitted an important point in my original post. In the dataset I'm working on, I have four groups. For one of the groups, one item is missing. I want to compare a model in which all parameters are constrained across groups (which runs fine) to a model in which the three groups with complete data have separate parameter estimates. Is there a way that I could reliably run this second model? Again, when I run this model, I get an estimate for the supposedly missing item/group and it's unclear where the estimate is coming from - it does not equal the estimate for any of the other groups. I obviously don't want a parameter estimate for the missing cell, but I would like trustworthy estimates for the three groups with complete data. To clarify, I've modified my example below.

library(mirt)

dat <- expand.table(LSAT6)

model <- "F = 1-5
CONSTRAIN = (1,2,3,4,5, a1)

CONSTRAINB = (1, d), (1,2,3,4,5, a1)"

## pretend that this is multiple group data
gp <- factor(rep(1:4, each = 250))

## suppose group 1 is not administered item 5
dat$Item_5[gp == 1] <- NA


mod <- multipleGroup(data = dat, model = model, group = gp,
                     invariance = c('free_means','free_var','slopes'),
technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'1'$items

coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'2'$items
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'3'$items
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'4'$items
## for group "1", gives an estimate for Item_5

Leah

P.S. Thanks for the tip about the standard errors.

I want to compare a model in which all parameters are constrained across groups (which runs fine) to a model in which the three groups with complete data have separate parameter estimates.
I think I follow you, but just to be clear does this mean you don't want to use any anchor items?

Is there a way that I could reliably run this second model? Again, when I run this model, I get an estimate for the supposedly missing item/group and it's unclear where the estimate is coming from - it does not equal the estimate for any of the other groups.

So, if you know that there is no information from these parameters then you might as well fix them to some constants, say 0 and 1 for the intercepts and slope, because it plays no part in the estimation (regardless of what you set them to the model will fit the same). Unfortunately the syntax doesn't make this very easy in MG models (I'll have to add support for that some time), so you have to do it the old fashioned way with the pars = 'values' approach and passing that data.frame back to the function.

I obviously don't want a parameter estimate for the missing cell, but I would like trustworthy estimates for the three groups with complete data. To clarify, I've modified my example below. 

library(mirt)

dat <- expand.table(LSAT6)

model <- "F = 1-5
          CONSTRAIN = (1,2,3,4,5, a1)
          CONSTRAINB = (1, d), (1,2,3,4,5, a1)"

## pretend that this is multiple group data
gp <- factor(rep(1:4, each = 250))

## suppose group 1 is not administered item 5
dat$Item_5[gp == 1] <- NA


mod <- multipleGroup(data = dat, model = model, group = gp,
                     invariance = c('free_means','free_var','slopes'),
                     technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))



coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'1'$items
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'2'$items
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'3'$items
coef(mod, simplify = TRUE)$'4'$items
## for group "1", gives an estimate for Item_5

Leah

P.S. Thanks for the tip about the standard errors.
